system:
You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",
 "summary": "<3-5 sentences: what happened or is expected, why, how sure>",
 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

response: {"headline":"HOPE-3 was a robust success: rosuvastatin significantly reduced cardiovascular events in 12,705 intermediate-risk patients, with an observed HR of about 0.77 matching the LDL-C-based prediction of 0.775.","summary":"The HOPE-3 trial randomized 12,705 participants without cardiovascular disease (men over 55, women over 60) to rosuvastatin or placebo and followed them for a median of 5.6 years. Both co-primary endpoints were met: the first was 3.7% versus 4.8% (HR about 0.77) and the second 4.4% versus 5.7% (HR about 0.77), a relative risk reduction of about 23%. The ACC readout concluded that lowering cholesterol with statins significantly reduced adverse cardiovascular events in intermediate-risk people with average cholesterol and blood pressure. The observed benefit matches the calculator's LDL-C-based expectation (HR 0.775, 22.5% RRR from a 1.024 mmol/L LDL-C reduction), and HMGCR genetics score 0.695 supports a causal target, so confidence is high despite the cutoff-timing caveat on genetic evidence.","key_evidence":["12,705 participants randomized (Novel Approaches in Primary Cardiovascular Disease Prevention: The HOPE-3 Trial Rationale, Design, and Participants' Baseline Characteristics; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00468923 HOPE-3; Study Supports Broader Use of Statins in Intermediate Risk Populations)","First co-primary endpoint: 3.7% rosuvastatin vs 4.8% placebo, HR about 0.77 (Study Supports Broader Use of Statins in Intermediate Risk Populations)","Second co-primary endpoint: 4.4% vs 5.7%, HR about 0.77 (Study Supports Broader Use of Statins in Intermediate Risk Populations)","Median follow-up 5.6 years (Study Supports Broader Use of Statins in Intermediate Risk Populations)","LDL-C reduced 25% (-39.6 mg/dL) within the rosuvastatin arm (Study Supports Broader Use of Statins in Intermediate Risk Populations)","Calculator expected HR 0.775 (22.5% RRR) based on LDL-C reduction of 1.024 mmol/L matches observed HR about 0.77 (calculator)","About 540 expected events exceeds 486 needed for 80% power (calculator note)","HMGCR genetic association score 0.695, above the >=0.5 causal threshold (opentargets:HMGCR)"],"what_would_change_this":"Nothing in the verified record would overturn the efficacy conclusion; the only caveat is methodological, since HMGCR genetic evidence post-dates the 2016-04-02 cutoff even though the score of 0.695 already supports causality. Longer follow-up or larger safety data could refine risk estimates but would not change the direction of the result.","readthrough_note":""}
